subject: ScaleBridge x Redwood — PromptKit / LangChain trace compatibility check
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@scalebridge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Li <devon@scalebridge.io>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: PromptKit + ScaleBridge compatibility w/ Redwood traces

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the runtime demo last week. ScaleBridge builds PromptKit (prompt authoring + runtime hooks) and were evaluating integration options to certify compatibility with Redwoods trace/telemetry model so our customers get end-to-end observability. High level: we want to make sure PromptKit can automatically annotate LangChain and LlamaIndex calls with trace IDs, surface token-level timings, and optionally ingest Redwoods trace telemetry for per-request debugging.

Can we confirm whether the following are supported or planned in Redwood:
- an ingestion endpoint for partner trace events (structured JSON with trace_id, span, timing)
- a lightweight client-side shim for LangChain that attaches Redwood request IDs to requests
- an approved pattern for attaching prompt/shot metadata without leaking sensitive user data

Devon (cc) is our eng lead and can share a short design doc / patch. Would love to get your engineering SME on a short compatibility check.

Best,
Ellen Park
Partnerships, ScaleBridge

Attachments: scalebridge-promptkit-arch.pdf (1.2MB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@scalebridge.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: PromptKit + ScaleBridge compatibility w/ Redwood traces

Ellen —

Thanks for the note and the PDF — we skimmed it and this looks promising. Quick answers up front:
- We dont currently expose a public partner ingestion endpoint for arbitrary trace events, but we have a partner-facing telemetry API in preview that accepts structured partner spans and associates them with Redwood request IDs.
- For LangChain/LlamaIndex, we have recommended shims and a TraceHook pattern in our SDKs that people use to propagate request IDs and token timing. The shim is typically a 8–12 line adapter.
- Regarding prompt metadata, we have PII-safe annotation guidelines: partners must strip or hash user identifiers and are limited to adding non-sensitive labels (experiment ids, prompt-template ids, etc.). We can share the compliance checklist.

Karthik and Kim — can one of you pick this up as the eng contact? Karthik, you know the LangChain trace hook best. Kim, can you check the telemetry ingestion preview constraints (rate limits, schema)?

Marissa
Director, ISV Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen@scalebridge.io>, Devon Li <devon@scalebridge.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: PromptKit + ScaleBridge compatibility w/ Redwood traces

Ellen / Devon —

I pulled the PDF. A few technical notes from the LangChain/LlamaIndex side:
1) LangChain instrumentation point: the best place is the LLM chain wrapper (we usually add a TraceHook around the LLM and the chain call). That lets us capture request_id, model, seq_len_in/seq_len_out, and per-token timestamps when streaming.
2) LlamaIndex: instrument at the service context layer to annotate index lookups and retrieval timings.
3) Telemetry ingestion preview: accepts newline-delimited JSON with the following minimal fields: trace_id, parent_id, span_name, start_ms, duration_ms, attributes. Rate limit is currently 200 rps per partner API key; we can request increases for pilot partners.

I've attached a small patch that shows how we add the trace_id to the LangChain request metadata and how we map streaming chunks to spans. Devon, if you can drop this into your sandbox and run a short trace capture I can validate quickly.

Attachments: tracehook-example.patch (text)

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime Integrations
From: Devon Li <devon@scalebridge.io>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: PromptKit + ScaleBridge compatibility w/ Redwood traces

Thanks Karthik —

We tried the patch in a small sandbox. A couple of follow-ups:
- The LangChain wrapper works, but our PromptKit runtime also does prompt-level transformations (templating and dynamic slot expansion) before the chain call. We need guidance on where to attach prompt_template_id and pre-expansion prompt text in the span so its visible in Redwood Console without showing raw user data.
- The streaming chunk timestamps are helpful; we noticed minor clock drift in one of our test VMs which made chunk ordering look odd in the trace UI. Is there a preferred best practice for normalizing timestamps before ingestion?

Wed like to run a short pilot (50k tokens/day) for two weeks if we can sort the annotation and timestamp guidance. I can share the sandbox logs and a minimal set of example traces.

—Devon
Eng Lead, ScaleBridge
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Li <devon@scalebridge.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: PromptKit + ScaleBridge compatibility w/ Redwood traces

Devon / team —

Great to hear you got the patch running. For your specific asks:
- Prompt metadata: please supply prompt_template_id (opaque string) and prompt_type (enum: user, system, assistant, transform). DO NOT supply raw user text in the span payload. If you need full prompts for quality debugging we can accept them via a secure upload workflow that redacts PII and requires an NDA/escrow key.
- Timestamp normalization: prefer server-side ingestion time as authoritative. Partners should include event_time_ms in the payload for ordering hints; Redwood will align by ingest_time_ms and surface both metrics in Console. Please avoid client-local clock reliance for ordering.
- Pilot: we can enable a partner preview key scoped to 100k tokens/day for 2 weeks. I created a HubSpot pilot entry and a shared Drive folder for sandbox traces (links below).

Next steps:
1) Devon: share 10 sample trace JSONs (anonymized) in the Drive folder and confirm sandbox API key request.
2) Marissa: Ill handoff to Partnerships for pilot MOU and technical kick.

Kim
Product Manager, Observability | Redwood Inference
